questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The FIFA World Cup (football) is held once every:
questions.explanation: The FIFA World Cup is held every 4 years. 2 years is wrong — that frequency applies to some continental championships; 3 years is wrong — no major football tournament follows this cycle; 5 years is wrong — exceeds the actual interval.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Olympic Games:

(i) The modern Olympic Games were revived in 1896 in Athens, Greece.
(ii) The Olympics are held every 4 years.
(iii) The five Olympic rings represent the five inhabited continents.
(iv) The Olympic Games have never been cancelled.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The modern Olympics began in Athens 1896 (i-correct); held every 4 years (ii-correct); five rings = five continents (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because the Olympics were cancelled in 1916 (WWI), 1940, and 1944 (WWII).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'LBW' in cricket stands for:
questions.explanation: LBW stands for Leg Before Wicket — a mode of dismissal when the ball hits the batsman's leg in line with the stumps. 'Left Before Wicket' is wrong — incorrect expansion; 'Long Ball Wide' is wrong — fabricated term; 'Last Batsman's Wicket' is wrong — not a cricket term.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cricket is the most popular sport in India.
Reason (R): India has won the Cricket World Cup multiple times and has produced legendary cricketers known worldwide.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Cricket is India's most popular sport by viewership and following (A is correct). India's World Cup wins (1983, 2011) and legendary players contribute to its popularity (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R partly explains A's popularity; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following trophies are associated with cricket?

(i) Ranji Trophy
(ii) Davis Cup
(iii) Duleep Trophy
(iv) Irani Cup

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Ranji Trophy (domestic first-class), Duleep Trophy (zonal), and Irani Cup (Ranji champion vs Rest of India) are all cricket tournaments (i, iii, iv correct). Davis Cup (ii) is wrong — it is an international tennis competition.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The sport of badminton originated in which country?
questions.explanation: Modern badminton originated in British India in the mid-19th century (Pune, then called Poona) and was later formalized in England. China is wrong — though dominant now, it's not the origin; England is wrong — the rules were formalized there but the game started in India; Japan is wrong — no historical connection to badminton's origin.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following sports with their associated terms:

Column I:
(a) Cricket
(b) Football
(c) Tennis
(d) Hockey

Column II:
(i) Penalty corner
(ii) Deuce
(iii) Hat-trick (originally)
(iv) Offside

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Hat-trick' originated in cricket (a-iii — a bowler taking 3 wickets in 3 balls earned a hat); 'offside' is a key football rule (b-iv); 'deuce' is a tennis term for 40-40 (c-ii); 'penalty corner' is in hockey (d-i). Option 2 swaps cricket and football; Option 3 swaps football and tennis; Option 4 swaps tennis and hockey.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The headquarters of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is located in:
questions.explanation: The IOC is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland. Paris is wrong — it hosts the 2024 Olympics but not the IOC HQ; New York is wrong — the UN is there, not IOC; London is wrong — no IOC connection.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Commonwealth Games:

(i) They are held every 4 years.
(ii) Only countries that were part of the British Empire participate.
(iii) India first participated in the Commonwealth Games in 1934.
(iv) The games were originally called the British Empire Games.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Commonwealth Games are held every 4 years (i-correct); India first participated in 1934 (iii-correct); originally called British Empire Games, started 1930 (iv-correct). Statement (ii) is wrong — Commonwealth membership (not just former Empire status) determines participation, and some members were never colonies.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The number of players in a standard football (soccer) team on the field is:
questions.explanation: A football team has 11 players on the field (including the goalkeeper). 9 is wrong — too few; 10 is wrong — one short of the standard; 12 is wrong — exceeds the standard team size.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Hockey is recognized as the national game of India.
Reason (R): India won six consecutive Olympic gold medals in hockey from 1928 to 1956.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Hockey is widely recognized as India's national game (A is correct). India did win six consecutive Olympic golds 1928-1956 (R is correct). However, R does not explain A because there is no official government notification declaring hockey as the national game — the recognition is traditional/popular, not caused by the Olympic wins specifically. Option 1 is wrong because the gold medals didn't 'cause' the designation; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Wimbledon Championships is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: Wimbledon is the oldest and most prestigious Grand Slam tennis tournament, held annually in London. Cricket is wrong — cricket has The Ashes, not Wimbledon; golf is wrong — golf has The Masters/The Open; badminton is wrong — badminton has the All England Open, not Wimbledon.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Grand Slam tennis tournaments?

(i) Australian Open
(ii) French Open (Roland Garros)
(iii) US Open
(iv) Indian Open

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The four Grand Slams are: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open (i, ii, iii correct). Indian Open (iv) is wrong — there is no Grand Slam called 'Indian Open'; the India Open is a badminton/golf tournament, not a tennis Grand Slam.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the highest individual award for lifetime achievement in sports given by the Government of India.
questions.explanation: The Major Dhyan Chand Award (formerly Dhyan Chand Award) is given for lifetime achievement in sports. Arjuna Award is wrong — it is for consistent outstanding performance over 4 years, not lifetime; Dronacharya Award is wrong — it is for coaches; Khel Ratna is wrong — it is for outstanding performance in recent years, not lifetime achievement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following sports personalities with their sports:

Column I:
(a) P.V. Sindhu
(b) Mary Kom
(c) Viswanathan Anand
(d) Neeraj Chopra

Column II:
(i) Javelin throw
(ii) Chess
(iii) Boxing
(iv) Badminton

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: P.V. Sindhu plays badminton (a-iv); Mary Kom is a boxer (b-iii); Viswanathan Anand is a chess grandmaster (c-ii); Neeraj Chopra is a javelin thrower (d-i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b); Option 3 swaps (c) and (d); Option 4 swaps (b) and (c).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'Grand Slam' in tennis refers to winning all four major tournaments in:
questions.explanation: A Grand Slam means winning all four major tournaments (Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, US Open) in the same calendar year. 'A career' is wrong — that is called a 'Career Grand Slam'; 'two consecutive years' is wrong — not the definition; 'three out of four' is wrong — all four are required.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021):

(i) India won its first-ever Olympic gold in athletics (javelin throw by Neeraj Chopra).
(ii) It was the first Olympics held without spectators in most venues.
(iii) India won a total of 7 medals at these Games.
(iv) The Games were postponed by one year due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won India's first athletics gold (i-correct); most venues had no spectators (ii-correct); India won 7 medals total (iii-correct — 1 gold, 2 silver, 4 bronze); the Games were postponed from 2020 to 2021 due to COVID (iv-correct). All four statements are factually accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Ashes' is a famous cricket series played between:
questions.explanation: The Ashes is a Test cricket series between England and Australia, dating back to 1882. India-Pakistan is wrong — their bilateral series has no such name; India-England is wrong — they play the Pataudi Trophy; South Africa-Australia is wrong — no 'Ashes' connection.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian Premier League (IPL) is one of the most-watched cricket leagues in the world.
Reason (R): IPL combines cricket with entertainment, short format (T20), and features top international players.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: IPL is among the most-watched cricket leagues globally (A is correct). Its T20 format, entertainment value, and international stars drive its popularity (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R explains the reasons for A; Option 3 is wrong because R is accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The total number of players in a standard volleyball team on the court is:
questions.explanation: A volleyball team has 6 players on the court at a time. 5 is wrong — that is basketball; 7 is wrong — that is kabaddi; 8 is wrong — exceeds volleyball's standard.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about kabaddi:

(i) It is a contact sport that originated in India.
(ii) Each team has 7 players on the court.
(iii) The raider must chant 'kabaddi' while in the opponent's half.
(iv) A standard kabaddi match has 4 quarters of 10 minutes each.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Kabaddi is an Indian contact sport (i-correct); 7 players per side (ii-correct); raiders must continuously chant 'kabaddi' (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because a standard kabaddi match has 2 halves of 20 minutes each, not 4 quarters.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The sport of polo is played on horseback. How many players are there in each polo team?
questions.explanation: Each polo team has 4 mounted players. 3 is wrong — too few for standard polo; 5 is wrong — exceeds team size; 6 is wrong — that is volleyball's team size.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following trophies/cups with their sports:

Column I:
(a) Thomas Cup
(b) Davis Cup
(c) Ryder Cup
(d) Stanley Cup

Column II:
(i) Ice Hockey
(ii) Golf
(iii) Tennis
(iv) Badminton

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Thomas Cup is for men's badminton (a-iv); Davis Cup is for men's tennis (b-iii); Ryder Cup is for golf (c-ii); Stanley Cup is for ice hockey (d-i). Option 2 swaps badminton and tennis; Option 3 swaps golf and ice hockey; Option 4 swaps tennis and golf.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cup titles in football?
questions.explanation: Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup 5 times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002), the most by any nation. Germany is wrong — 4 titles; Argentina is wrong — 3 titles; Italy is wrong — 4 titles.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The standard duration of a one-day international (ODI) cricket match is __________ overs per side.
questions.explanation: An ODI match consists of 50 overs per side. 20 overs is wrong — that is T20 format; 40 overs is wrong — no standard format uses this; 60 overs is wrong — exceeds the ODI limit.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following Indian sportspersons have won Olympic gold medals?

(i) Abhinav Bindra (Shooting, 2008)
(ii) Neeraj Chopra (Javelin, 2020)
(iii) Saina Nehwal (Badminton, 2012)
(iv) The Indian Hockey Team (1980)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won gold in shooting 2008 Beijing (i-correct); Neeraj Chopra won gold in javelin 2020 Tokyo (ii-correct); Indian Hockey team won gold in 1980 Moscow (iv-correct). Saina Nehwal (iii) is wrong — she won a bronze medal in 2012 London, not gold.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Summer Olympic Games 2024 were held in which city?
questions.explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France. Tokyo is wrong — that hosted the 2020/2021 Olympics; Los Angeles is wrong — it will host 2028; London is wrong — it hosted 2012.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the sport of wrestling:

(i) It is one of the oldest sports, featured in the ancient Olympic Games.
(ii) Freestyle and Greco-Roman are the two Olympic styles.
(iii) In Greco-Roman wrestling, holds below the waist are allowed.
(iv) India has won Olympic medals in wrestling.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Wrestling was in ancient Olympics (i-correct); freestyle and Greco-Roman are Olympic styles (ii-correct); India has won Olympic wrestling medals — Sushil Kumar, Sakshi Malik, Bajrang Punia, Ravi Dahiya (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because in Greco-Roman wrestling, holds below the waist are NOT allowed — that is the key distinction from freestyle.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Super Over' in cricket is used to:
options: Decide the winner when a match ends in a tie
Penalize a team for slow over-rate
Determine the Man of the Match
Award bonus runs to the batting team
questions.correctAnswer: Decide the winner when a match ends in a tie
questions.explanation: A Super Over is a tiebreaker used in limited-overs cricket when the scores are level after regulation play. Penalizing slow over-rate is wrong — that involves fines/suspensions; bonus runs is wrong — no such mechanism; Man of the Match is wrong — that is decided by judges.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India hosted the Asian Games in 1951 and 1982.
Reason (R): New Delhi has the infrastructure and experience to host large multi-sport events.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India did host Asian Games in 1951 (first ever) and 1982 in New Delhi (A is correct). Delhi has sports infrastructure (R is correct). However, R does not explain A because India hosted in 1951 BEFORE major infrastructure existed — the 1951 hosting was due to India's initiative in founding the Asian Games, not existing infrastructure. Option 1 is wrong because R doesn't causally explain A; Option 3 is wrong because R is correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'hat-trick' in football refers to:
options: Scoring 3 goals by the same player in a single match
questions.correctAnswer: Scoring 3 goals by the same player in a single match
questions.explanation: A hat-trick in football is when one player scores three goals in a single match. 2 goals is wrong — that is called a 'brace'; winning 3 matches is wrong — that is a winning streak; corner kicks is wrong — no such term exists.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Khelo India programme:

(i) It is a Government of India initiative to promote sports at grassroots level.
(ii) It provides annual scholarships to talented young athletes.
(iii) It includes the Khelo India Youth Games and University Games.
(iv) It is managed by the International Olympic Committee.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Khelo India is a government programme for grassroots sports (i-correct); provides scholarships to athletes (ii-correct); includes Youth Games and University Games (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Khelo India is managed by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India — not by the IOC.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following countries with sports they are most famous for:

Column I:
(a) Brazil
(b) New Zealand
(c) China
(d) Canada

Column II:
(i) Table Tennis
(ii) Ice Hockey
(iii) Rugby (All Blacks)
(iv) Football (Soccer)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Brazil is football-famous (a-iv); New Zealand's All Blacks are rugby legends (b-iii); China dominates table tennis (c-i); Canada is famous for ice hockey (d-ii). Option 2 swaps Brazil and NZ; Option 3 swaps China and Canada; Option 4 swaps NZ and China.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Tour de France' is a famous sporting event associated with:
questions.explanation: The Tour de France is the world's most prestigious multi-stage cycling race. Motor racing is wrong — that is Formula 1 or Le Mans; marathon running is wrong — marathons are single-day events; swimming is wrong — no such event in swimming.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following sports use a shuttlecock?

(i) Badminton
(ii) Table Tennis
(iii) Lawn Tennis
(iv) Squash

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Only badminton uses a shuttlecock (feathered or synthetic projectile). Table tennis (ii) is wrong — it uses a small plastic ball; lawn tennis (iii) is wrong — it uses a felt-covered rubber ball; squash (iv) is wrong — it uses a small rubber ball.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) The Olympic motto is 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' meaning 'Faster, Higher, Stronger'.
(ii) 'Communiter' (Together) was added to the motto in 2021.
(iii) The Olympic flame is lit in Athens, Greece before each Games.
(iv) Pierre de Coubertin is the founder of the modern Olympic Games.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The original motto is 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' (i-correct); 'Communiter' was added in 2021 making it 'Faster, Higher, Stronger — Together' (ii-correct); the flame is lit at Olympia, Greece (iii-correct — ancient Olympia, which is in Greece); Pierre de Coubertin founded the modern Olympics (iv-correct). All four are factually accurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's medal tally at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics:

| Medal | Count |
|-------|-------|
| Gold | 1 |
| Silver | 2 |
| Bronze | 4 |

What was India's total medal count at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics?
questions.explanation: Total = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 medals. 5 is wrong (underestimates); 6 is wrong (miscounts); 8 is wrong (overcounts).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sachin Tendulkar is called the 'God of Cricket'.
Reason (R): He holds the record for most runs in both Test and ODI cricket and has scored 100 international centuries.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Sachin is widely known as 'God of Cricket' (A is correct). His record-breaking run tallies and 100 centuries explain why he earned this title (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains A; Option 3 is wrong because R is accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The sport of 'kho-kho' originated in:
questions.explanation: Kho-kho is an ancient Indian sport with roots in Maharashtra, dating back to the Deccan region. Pakistan is wrong — no historical origin connection; Sri Lanka is wrong — it originated in India; Bangladesh is wrong — no historical connection to kho-kho's origins.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following sports with the number of players per team on the field:

Column I:
(a) Cricket
(b) Basketball
(c) Hockey
(d) Kabaddi

Column II:
(i) 7
(ii) 11
(iii) 5
(iv) 11

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Cricket has 11 players (a-ii); basketball has 5 (b-iii); hockey has 11 (c-iv); kabaddi has 7 (d-i). Option 2 wrongly assigns 5 to cricket; Option 3 assigns 7 to hockey; Option 4 reverses all assignments.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'ace' in tennis refers to:
options: A point won after a long rally
A serve that the receiver fails to touch
A double fault by the opponent
questions.correctAnswer: A serve that the receiver fails to touch
questions.explanation: An ace is a serve that lands in the service box and is not touched by the receiver, winning the point outright. 'Long rally' is wrong — no specific term for that; 'winning 6-0' is wrong — that is a 'bagel'; 'double fault' is wrong — that is when the server faults on both attempts.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the World Cup cricket:

(i) The first Cricket World Cup was held in 1975 in England.
(ii) India won the Cricket World Cup in 1983 under Kapil Dev.
(iii) Australia has won the most Cricket World Cup titles.
(iv) The World Cup is held every 2 years.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: First World Cup in 1975, England (i-correct); India won in 1983 under Kapil Dev (ii-correct); Australia has won 6 titles, the most (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because the Cricket World Cup is held every 4 years, not 2.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The sport in which 'try', 'scrum', and 'lineout' are common terms is:
questions.explanation: Try (scoring by grounding the ball), scrum (a method of restarting play), and lineout (throw-in from the sideline) are all rugby terms. Football is wrong — it uses 'goal', 'corner', 'throw-in'; hockey is wrong — it uses 'bully', 'penalty corner'; baseball is wrong — it uses 'home run', 'innings', 'strike'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows venues of the last few Olympic Games:

| Year | City |
|------|------|
| 2008 | Beijing |
| 2012 | London |
| 2016 | Rio de Janeiro |
| 2020 | Tokyo |
| 2024 | Paris |

How many years separate the Beijing Olympics from the Paris Olympics?
questions.explanation: 2024 − 2008 = 16 years between Beijing and Paris Olympics. 12 years is wrong (2008 to 2020); 14 years is wrong (miscalculation); 18 years is wrong (2008 to 2026, not applicable).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following sports are included in the Summer Olympics?

(i) Athletics
(ii) Swimming
(iii) Ice skating
(iv) Wrestling

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Athletics (i-correct), swimming (ii-correct), and wrestling (iv-correct) are all Summer Olympic sports. Ice skating (iii) is wrong because it is a Winter Olympic sport, not included in the Summer Games.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Uber Cup' is an international tournament associated with:
questions.explanation: The Uber Cup is the premier international women's team badminton championship. Men's badminton is wrong — that is the Thomas Cup; men's tennis is wrong — that is the Davis Cup; women's tennis is wrong — that is the Billie Jean King Cup (formerly Fed Cup).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Major Dhyan Chand:

(i) He was one of the greatest hockey players in history.
(ii) He scored over 400 goals in his international career.
(iii) India's National Sports Day (29 August) is celebrated on his birthday.
(iv) He played for the Indian football team.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Dhyan Chand was a legendary hockey player (i-correct); scored over 400 international goals (ii-correct); 29 August (his birthday) is National Sports Day (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Dhyan Chand was a HOCKEY player, not a football player.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's Cricket World Cup wins:

| Year | Venue | Format |
|------|-------|--------|
| 1983 | England | ODI |
| 2007 | South Africa | T20 |
| 2011 | India | ODI |

How many years elapsed between India's first and second ODI World Cup victory?
questions.explanation: First ODI World Cup win: 1983. Second ODI World Cup win: 2011. Gap = 2011 − 1983 = 28 years. 24 years is wrong (would be 2007); 26 years is wrong (would be 2009); 30 years is wrong (would be 2013).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following sports events with their host cities in 2024-2026:

Column I:
(a) 2024 Summer Olympics
(b) 2024 T20 World Cup (Cricket)
(c) 2026 FIFA World Cup
(d) 2028 Summer Olympics

Column II:
(i) USA, Canada, Mexico (jointly)
(ii) Paris
(iii) Los Angeles
(iv) USA and West Indies (jointly)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 2024 Olympics in Paris (a-ii); 2024 T20 WC in USA and West Indies (b-iv); 2026 FIFA WC in USA/Canada/Mexico (c-i); 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles (d-iii). Option 2 swaps (c) and (d); Option 3 swaps (a) and (b); Option 4 swaps (b) and (c).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'marathon' in athletics refers to a foot race covering a distance of approximately:
questions.explanation: A marathon covers 42.195 km (26.2 miles). 21 km is wrong — that is a half-marathon; 35 km is wrong — no standard race at this distance; 50 km is wrong — that is a race walking event, not a standard marathon.
